hints.title: Last Occurrence Boundary Expansion
hints.text: Each partition must contain all occurrences of every character that appears inside it. How can the last occurrence of each character define partition boundaries?

hints.title: Furthest Character Index Window Invariant
hints.text: The current partition must extend at least to the furthest last appearance of any character seen so far in the partition.

hints.title: Running Maximum Boundary Cut Procedure
hints.text: Record the last index of every character in a lookup table. Scan the string while updating the running boundary to the maximum last occurrence of current characters. When the index matches this boundary, close the partition, record its length, and begin the next.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input array length or bit count
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Merging intervals without precomputing last occurrences leads to repeated substring scans.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single lookup pass of 26 characters allows a linear scan to partition the string in O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that a partition can end as soon as the current index equals the maximum last seen position.
